segments.text: A proton beam goes straight through his head. In at the back. Out beside his nose. He feels no pain.
Through his head? No chance. Let's go look.
{1978|Nineteen seventy eight}. Anatoli Bugorski is a physicist at the biggest particle accelerator in the Soviet Union. Something breaks. He leans in to check.
But a safety mechanism has failed. The beam is still on. He sees a flash, by his account brighter than a thousand suns.
He finishes his work. Then the left side of his face swells up.
Doctors in Moscow expect him to die. By some estimates, the dose is hundreds of times a lethal one.
He doesn't. He loses the hearing in his left ear, and half his face is paralysed. But he finishes his doctorate, and goes back to work at the same accelerator.
A beam through the brain. And he went back to work. I was wrong. Case closed.
